name: Binance BTC/USDT short-horizon realized volatility
description: One-second causal observations of the fresh Binance displayed best-quote midpoint are converted to simple basis-point returns. volatility_bps_15s and volatility_bps_60s are the root mean square of the latest 15 and 60 returns. short_long_ratio is the 15-return value divided by the 60-return value; when both windows have zero root-mean-square volatility, the ratio is defined as 1 and regime is stable. Regime is contracting at or below 0.8, expanding at or above 1.2, and stable between those boundaries. The 0.8 and 1.2 regime boundaries are initial research thresholds that require empirical calibration; the return and root-mean-square formulas are not heuristic thresholds. Any missing or stale one-second Binance midpoint observation breaks continuity and restarts the 60-return warm-up. This identity is single-venue: it reads only Binance inputs and is ready whenever the Binance midpoint ring holds 61 contiguous one-second samples, independently of the other adopted spot venue. The blended `btc.external.*` reading of the same measurement stays the reference layer and continues to require every adopted venue (ADR 0024). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even. Venue port (B1): this identity is the Binance sibling of `btc.coinbase.realized_volatility@1.0.0` and reuses that definition's formulas, windows, thresholds, warm-up, staleness bound, field set, field types and eight-place round-half-to-even rounding verbatim; only the source ids differ (`crates/btc-signals/src/spot_signals.rs`, `crates/btc-signals/src/candidate_spot_signals.rs`). The instrument is Binance spot BTCUSDT; this identity publishes no price-level field, so its outputs (base sizes, basis points, imbalances, ratios, counts) are quote-currency neutral and nothing is converted. Binance inputs are rights-gated (`signals/knowledge/RIGHTS-LEDGER.md`): the lane is built and tested to the adopted standard, and its runtime refuses to start unless the environment allow-list `SIGNALS_ENABLED_VENUES` names `binance`, which the deployment sets only after that row clears. The Binance quote input is the `btcusdt@bookTicker` stream, which publishes the best bid and ask price and quantity on every best-quote change. It is the Binance analogue of the Coinbase ticker's displayed best quote; the `depth20` top of book is explicitly NOT used as a second quote source. quote_currency is emitted on every decision and is the constant "usd" for this venue: this identity publishes no price-denominated field — its outputs are base sizes, ratios, basis-point and count fields, all quote-currency neutral — so nothing is converted. Wire contract status (E45b): this identity reads only binance.spot.btcusdt.book-ticker, whose live payload was absent from the wave-A capture; its contract, documented ahead of observation, is now observed and confirmed against a fresh gated Binance spot capture (binance-spot-r2-20260903T235740Z, 2026-09-03, 454344 `btcusdt@bookTicker` frames carrying the u/s/b/B/a/A best-quote fields and no engine timestamp). E47 (USD quoting): this identity quotes in USD and publishes no price, notional or quote-denominated cost field — its outputs are base sizes, counts, basis-point ratios and durations, which are quote-currency neutral — so nothing is converted and no usdt_usd_rate is published. quote_currency is the constant "usd".
